amounts.name: Cap on total Income Tax losses claimable against a year's income
amounts.value: £50,000, or 25% of that income if greater

caveats: Relief cannot be restricted to preserve personal Income Tax allowances - the loss is deducted from total income before allowances.
If Income Tax relief is claimed for a capital loss, it cannot also be set against capital gains.
The £50,000/25% of income limit does not apply to losses on shares with EIS or SEIS relief attributable.
There is a specified order of priority for losses claimed in a tax year (share losses in-year first, then carried-back share losses, then other Income Tax losses).
If claiming for multiple tax years, the claim must state which year takes priority.

note.summary: This chunk explains how and when to claim Income Tax relief for an allowable capital loss on qualifying shares, including the one-year time limit from 31 January following the loss year, the specific SA108/SA110 boxes to use for 2025-26 and 2024-25 claims, and required minimum information about the issuing company. It also describes how relief is given (deducted from total income before personal allowances, with an ordering priority for losses), and sets out the £50,000 or 25% of income cap on total Income Tax losses claimable, with a worked example (Example 6).

amounts.name: Example 4 - subscription for shares / allowable capital loss claimed

caveats: This helpsheet explains the basic rules for tax year 2025 to 2026 and does not cover all scenarios; complex cases may need a tax adviser.
If Making Tax Digital for Income Tax applies, claims and adjustments are made through compatible software instead of the Self Assessment boxes referenced in this helpsheet.
You cannot make a negligible value claim after the company has been dissolved; you are instead automatically treated as having disposed of the shares at the time of dissolution.
A gift of shares is not a qualifying disposal for share loss relief purposes.
The date chosen for a deemed disposal in a negligible value claim could affect ability to claim some other reliefs.
Delay in submitting the claim/tax return affects how far back the earlier specified time can be set.

definitions.meaning: An asset is of negligible value if it is worth next to nothing.

A claim to set certain allowable capital losses on disposal of shares subscribed for in a qualifying trading company against income, rather than only against chargeable gains.

note.summary: This HS286 helpsheet (2025 to 2026 tax year) explains how to make a negligible value claim on an asset that has become worthless, and how to claim Share Loss Relief to set allowable capital losses on disposal of subscriber shares in qualifying trading companies against Income Tax. It sets out conditions for a competent negligible value claim (must still own the asset when claiming, asset became negligible while owned), how far back an earlier specified disposal date can go, and how to notify HMRC of the resulting allowable loss via SA108 boxes with code 'NVC' or 'MUL'. It also covers using form CG34 to check valuations and lists qualifying disposal types for share loss relief.

e064e23618a96eae.heading: Negligible value claims and Income Tax losses on disposal of shares (Self Assessment helpsheet HS286) > In what type of company should I have subscribed for shares

amounts.name: Gross assets limit (shares issued before 6 April 2006)
amounts.value: £15 million immediately before, £16 million immediately after the issue

amounts.name: Gross assets limit (shares issued on or after 6 April 2006)
amounts.value: £7 million immediately before, £8 million immediately after the issue

amounts.name: Limit on Income Tax reliefs
amounts.value: £50,000, or 25% of your income if that is greater

amounts.name: Example 5 - EIS relief claimed vs loss relief
amounts.value: Subscribed £10,000, EIS relief £2,000 (20%), loss relief claimable £8,000

amounts.name: Substantial non-qualifying activity threshold
amounts.ref: In what type of company should I have subscribed for shares

caveats: Rules differ significantly depending on whether shares were issued before or on/after 6 April 1998, and gross assets limits differ depending on whether issued before or on/after 6 April 2006.
The £50,000/25% of income limit on Income Tax reliefs does not apply to losses on shares to which EIS or SEIS relief is attributable.
Relief on shares acquired via reorganisation or share exchange is only available in limited circumstances unless ownership of the new company exactly mirrors the old company.
No relief for losses on shares in the holding company of a non-trading group.

Where a shareholding includes both subscribed and non-subscribed (bought/gifted/inherited) shares, only the subscribed portion qualifies and apportionment rules apply — reader advised to seek further guidance.

definitions.meaning: Must not exceed gross assets limit in force at issue; must not be listed on a recognised stock exchange (or have arrangements to be) at issue, unless listed on or after 7 March 2001; must not be a building society or registered industrial and provident society; must be a trading company (wholly for qualifying trades, or group with non-qualifying activities not substantial, i.e. broadly not more than ~20%)

definitions.term: Qualifying trading company (shares issued before 6 April 1998)

definitions.meaning: Trade consisting wholly or mainly of dealing in shares, securities, land, or commodity futures; or not pursued on a commercial basis expected to make a profit
definitions.ref: Trading companies that do not qualify

definitions.term: How long must the company have been a trading company

definitions.meaning: Relief still available if company stopped trading no more than 3 years before disposal, has not started a non-qualifying activity, and satisfied qualifying conditions at date it stopped trading

Must not be fixed rate dividend preference shares; must have been subscribed for individually (including jointly or via nominee); shares transferred from a spouse/civil partner during their lifetime who subscribed for them are treated as subscribed for by the recipient; subscribed shares are those issued for money or money's worth

note.summary: This chunk sets out detailed conditions a company must satisfy to be a 'qualifying trading company' for the purpose of claiming Income Tax loss relief on negligible value or disposal of subscribed shares, with different rules depending on whether shares were issued before or after 6 April 1998. It covers the gross assets rule thresholds, disqualifying trades, the 6-year trading requirement, treatment of companies that have stopped trading, share reorganisations/takeovers, and how to calculate the allowable loss including interaction with EIS relief and the £50,000/25% of income limit on Income Tax reliefs.
